s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of fever and generalized skin eruption with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face
Large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
key_facts: Recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 81 K/μL
Hypocomplementemia with C3 of 42 mg/dL and C4 of 3 mg/dL
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of fever and generalized skin eruption with mucosal involvement and target lesions

shortlist.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Widespread skin necrosis and detachment with fever and recent history of photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: History of SLE with recent flare and current presentation of fever, skin eruption, and positive autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of ACLE and current presentation of fever, skin eruption, and positive autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of bullae and target lesions with a history of SLE and positive autoantibodies

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, generalized eruption, and target lesions, along with the presence of bullae and mucosal involvement, is consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. The recent history of photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and the positive autoantibody profile also support this diagnosis, as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome can be triggered by systemic lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: While the patient has widespread skin lesions and bullae, the presence of target lesions and the lack of extensive epidermal detachment make Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis less likely.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, the current presentation is more consistent with a specific cutaneous manifestation, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, rather than a flare of systemic lupus erythematosus itself.

rejected.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and the presence of typical lesions of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus are noted, but the current presentation with target lesions, bullae, and systemic symptoms is more suggestive of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

rejected.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has bullae, the overall clinical presentation and the presence of target lesions are more consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome than bullous lupus erythematosus.
